text.aria-label: Title text 'Figure 13: Describing each plant to a shared XGBoost model lowers error, less so for an unseen plant'
text.tspan: Figure 13: Describing each plant to a shared XGBoost model lowers error,
less so for an unseen plant

text.aria-label: Subtitle text 'Every row is one XGBoost model shared by all plants, scored by mean absolute error at lead-day 1 (the forecast for the day after the day it is issued). The fingerprint (G-FP) describes each plant by its transfer ratio (TF), clipping ceiling (CK), and daily shape. An unseen plant is a plant left out of training (the leave-one-plant-out, LOPO, rows). A post hoc decomposition in the follow-up report attributes the gain to the transfer ratio, and finds the clipping ceiling does not help a plant the model has not seen. Dot: estimate. Line: 95% interval from resampling whole months. All rows are exploratory. Arms. G-B0: one global XGBoost model with no plant information. G-ID: one global model given a plant code. G-L1: one global model given L1. G-FP: one global model given the plant's TF, CK, and daily shape (a fingerprint). LOPO: leave one plant out, meaning the scored plant is left out of training. TF: the 30-day ratio of power to forecast irradiance (the transfer ratio). CK: the plant's clipping ceiling.'
